body: Operator report: last night's job never ran, but the dashboard showed success. app/scheduler.py run_once(state, today, job) catches a transient exception from job(), then still records state['last_completed'] = today and returns 'ran', so every later invocation that day returns 'already-ran' and the work silently skips. Fix run_once() so a raising job returns 'failed', does NOT set last_completed (a later same-day invocation must retry the job), and does not propagate the exception; a successful retry then returns 'ran' and marks completion. The already-completed-today skip and the successful path stay exactly as they are. Acceptance: failing job -> 'failed' with last_completed unchanged; failing then succeeding invocations on the same day -> 'failed' then 'ran'; existing tests still pass.
title: Nightly job silently skips after a transient failure
